body.p: The present application includes claims 1-20. Claims 5, 9, 11, 15, 18, and 20 have been amended. New claims 21 and 22 have been added.1
Claims 5, 9, 11, 15, 17, 18, and 20 were objected to due to informalities. The claims have been clarified to render the objections moot.

Claims 1-6, 9, 10, and 12-19 were rejected as being unpatentable over U.S. 3,848,832 ("Stanley") in view of U.S. 2022/0033060 ("Behzadpour"). Claim 1 recites, in part, "one or more splice straps that secure the one or more struts to the wing." Claims 13 and 18 recite similar limitations.
The claims are clear that the splice strap(s) secure strut(s) to a wing. The claims do not recite that the splice strap(s) secure a first strut to a second strut.

The Office Action acknowledges that Stanely does not describe, teach, or suggest "one or more splice straps that secure the one or more struts to the wing." See March 6, 2024 Office Action at pages 5, 8, and 11. In an attempt to overcome these acknowledged deficiencies, the
Office Action relies on Behzadpour. See id.

However, Behzadpour discloses spar splice plates 216 and 218 that couple two spars together. See Behzadpour at [0114]. In particular, Behzadpour discloses the "outer wing front spar 212 and the outer wing rear spar 214 may extend continuously between the outer wing stout rib 232 and the wing tip 126, and may also be coupled (e.g., via spar splice plates 216, 218) respectively to the center wing front spar 152 and center wing rear spar 154 ...." See id.

As shown in Figure 5 (reproduced below), in particular, the spar splice plate 216 couples to front faces of the center wing front spar 152 and the outer wing front spar 212, while the spar splice plate 218 couples to rear faces of the center wing front spar 152 and the outer wing front
spar 212.

Again, the spar splice plates of Behzadpour connect two spars together. See id at [0114], [0138], [0164], and Figure 5. Like Stanley, Behzadpour also does not expressly or necessarily describe, teach, or suggest splice straps that secure a strut to a wing.
Additionally, claim 6 recites, in part, "one or more upper splice straps extending over a

first top surface of a rear end of the one or more struts and a second top surface of a front end of the one or more ribs; and one or more lower splice straps extending over a first bottom surface of the rear end of the one or more struts and a second bottom surface of the front end of the one or more ribs." Claims 16 and 19 recite similar limitations.

The Office Action acknowledges that Stanely does not expressly or necessarily describe, teach, or suggest these limitations. See March 6, 2024 Office Action at pages 5, 8, and 11. As such, the Office Action relies on Behzadpour. See id.

However, as explained above, Behzadpour discloses spar splice plates 216 and 218 on front faces and rear faces, respectively, of spars. The spar splice plates of Behzadpour are not disposed over top surfaces or below bottom of anything, in general, and certainly not over or below struts and/or ribs.

Neither Stanely, nor Behzadpour (alone or in combination with one another) describes, teaches, or suggests "one or more upper splice straps extending over a first top surface of a rear end of the one or more struts and a second top surface of a front end of the one or more ribs; and one or more lower splice straps extending over a first bottom surface of the rear end of the one or more struts and a second bottom surface of the front end of the one or more ribs," as recited in claim 6, for example. For at least these additional reasons, the proposed combination does not render claims 6, 16, and 19 unpatentable.

Claims 7, 8, and 20 were rejected as being unpatentable over Stanley in view of Behzadpour and U.S. 5,524,847 ("Brodell"). Claim 11 was rejected as being unpatentable over Stanely in view of Behzadpour and CN 201660965 ("Liu"). The Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of these rejections for at least the reasons set forth with respect to Stanley and Behzadpour.

In general, the Office Action makes various statements regarding the pending claims and the cited references that are now moot in light of the above. Thus, the Applicant will not address such statements at the present time. However, the Applicant expressly reserves the right to challenge such statements in the future should the need arise (e.g., if such statements should become relevant by appearing in a rejection of any current or future claim).
The Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the claim rejections for at least the reasons discussed above. If the Examiner has any questions or the Applicant can be of any
assistance, the Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned attorney.
